title: Outcomes and Survey Improvement

decisionLog.outcome: Reconstructed 2.4.4 around three connected work packages: student proposition and adoption; external reputation and market activation; and strategic survey performance and reputation optimisation. Year 1 will prove the operating model, prioritising internal proposition work and targeted Graduate Outcomes response-rate optimisation while 2.4.1 builds the graduate premium evidence and content estate. Year 2 scales student adoption and tests targeted external activation; Year 3 embeds the strongest approaches and builds sustained reputation and survey-performance capability. Headline resourcing assumes 0.5 FTE dedicated activation/reputation delivery capacity in 2026/27, rising to 1.0 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29, alongside existing shared King's Edge analytics, project-officer and programme-management capacity and an indicative flexible activation/research envelope of £25,000, £50,000 and £75,000. The precise role design, analytical requirement and business-as-usual destination remain to be validated during proposition review.

Added a programme-controlled Strategic Partnerships, Profile & External Engagement Fund to 2.4.4 as the single accounting home for flexible external-engagement investment deployable across King's Edge. The fund is £25,000 in 2026/27, £35,000 in 2027/28 and £45,000 in 2028/29, with a £45,000 annual recurrent BAU planning liability from 2029/30. It is additional to the existing activation, research and survey-intervention envelopes and must not be double counted against 2.2.2 partnership infrastructure or other package budgets.

decisionLog.forum: King's Edge and Digital Student Experience Hub resource alignment
decisionLog.outcome: Retained the existing 2.4.4 activation/reputation allocation and its King’s Edge accounting profile, but agreed that the eventual post design should be broader than a narrowly dedicated communications role. Organisationally the 2.4.4 allocation should be designed alongside the additional 0.5 FTE content-design/editorial provision funded through 4.1.1, creating a combined King’s Edge / Student Experience communications and content capability of approximately 1.0 FTE in 2026/27 and 1.5 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29. The two funding asks remain separate and auditable: 2.4.4 continues to carry its existing King’s Edge share and 4.1.1 carries the additional Hub share.

Rebased the recommended core case for 2.4.4 while protecting the evidence, survey-optimisation and strategic external-engagement functions. Dedicated activation/reputation delivery remains 0.5 FTE in 2026/27 and is now 0.75 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29 rather than 1.0 FTE. The activation/research/survey-intervention envelopes remain £25,000 in Year 1 and are now £35,000 and £50,000 in Years 2 and 3. The Strategic Partnerships, Profile & External Engagement Fund remains £25,000 / £35,000 / £45,000 with a £45,000 BAU planning liability. Organisational alignment with the separate 4.1.1 0.5 FTE content provision remains, creating approximately 1.0 FTE combined capacity in 2026/27 and 1.25 FTE in 2027/28 and 2028/29 before other institutional contributions.

Specified the first concrete Graduate Outcomes response-rate campaign test within the existing Year 1 optimisation model: ten short campaign video assets, produced through the 2.4.1 content-production route, combined with paid targeted LinkedIn activity focused on priority graduate cohorts identified through response and outcomes intelligence. The intervention should be evaluated as a test of whether targeted paid social and tailored creative improve response in high-value cohorts rather than treated as a generic communications campaign.
decisionLog.notes: The proposed pre-business-case media/campaign funding is an early release against existing Year 1 2.4.1 production and 2.4.4 activation/survey-intervention envelopes. Asset production remains accounted for in 2.4.1; paid targeting, campaign operation and evaluation remain accounted for in 2.4.4.

caseForChange.problem: Survey response and reputation performance are not yet managed consistently as strategic evidence and improvement cycles.
caseForChange.opportunity: Targeted Graduate Outcomes and priority survey interventions improve representation, insight and institutional decisions.
caseForChange.whyNow: A first Graduate Outcomes intervention can be tested while the broader evidence estate develops.
caseForChange.intendedChange: Targeted Graduate Outcomes and priority survey interventions improve representation, insight and institutional decisions.

summary: Improves Graduate Outcomes response and establishes a focused annual strategy for priority outcomes, employability and reputation surveys.
detailSummary: Understand target populations, survey mechanics, response patterns and the few institutional measures with material outcomes or reputation value. Start with targeted Graduate Outcomes response-rate interventions where positive destinations are strong but response is weaker than expected; evaluate effect before scaling. Extend to priority external employability and reputation surveys with explicit ownership and an annual evaluate-and-refine cycle. The existing shared analytics allocation moves here from the integrated V1 deliverable. The combined activation, research and survey-intervention cash envelope is held once by Student and External Activation until the survey share can be costed without inventing an allocation.
problemSolved: Survey response and reputation performance are not yet managed consistently as strategic evidence and improvement cycles.
whatChanges: Targeted Graduate Outcomes and priority survey interventions improve representation, insight and institutional decisions.

components.title: WP3 · Strategic Survey Performance and Reputation Optimisation
components.summary: Systematically improve performance in high-value outcomes and reputation surveys by understanding how each instrument works and applying targeted interventions, beginning with Graduate Outcomes response-rate optimisation and priority employability and reputation surveys.
